1:_: That has three partitions. In Tur it is written here that it is complete reshut ha-yachid from the Torah, and Beit Yosef questioned: behold in siman 345 Tur wrote that mavo'ot that have three partitions and no lechi and korah on the fourth side are like karmelit; and he answered that what he said here complete reshut ha-yachid is not to make one who throws into it from reshut ha-rabbim liable but to permit carrying within it etc., for such is the law of karmelit from the Torah etc., and this is strained; for behold he said here complete reshut ha-yachid; and in my humble opinion to answer: in siman 345 it deals that the fourth opening is to reshut ha-rabbim as he wrote there, and the corners adjacent to reshut ha-rabbim such as mavo'ot that have three partitions etc.; and this mavo sometimes the public press to enter there when there are many people in reshut ha-rabbim as stated in the Gemara chapter 1 of Shabbos daf 10 — therefore even though by itself it is complete reshut ha-yachid nevertheless reshut ha-rabbim nullifies it from being reshut ha-yachid but it is called side of reshut ha-rabbim and is like karmelit; unlike here where we do not deal with this matter that the public press there sometimes — it remains on it the name complete reshut ha-yachid from the Torah even though he said here wherever there are three partitions etc.; and this is in Mehadrin part 17; and the wording of Knesset HaMelekh that Tur mentioned implies even open to reshut ha-rabbim and this is where the public do not press there; and understand that wherever Tur stated it refers to courtyard and mavo:
2:א: A courtyard fully breached etc. — meaning square; but mavo its length is more than its width:
2:ב: A tefach from here. — it implies there is a difference between making a pas — then two mashehuyin suffice as he mentioned first; but in what remained a tefach is required and this was not mentioned in Beit Yosef — on the contrary he wrote the opposite on the words of R' Yehuda; except that Tosafos chapter 1 daf 10 wrote to distinguish thus; end of his words; and Beit Yosef himself brought this afterward:
7:_: And therefore they make lechi from smeared plaster etc. — and even though in Terumat HaDeshen he wrote that lechi that if wind blows on it cannot stand is invalid — and here certainly the plaster cannot stand — there it deals with lechi that is valid by itself for mavo without tzurat hapetach that requires some measure; but here what they make from smeared plaster is for tzurat hapetach that requires only one reed from here and one reed from here suffices in whatever amount; and this is the difference in Terumat HaDeshen siman 74; and accordingly Rama's words are not resolved that wrote and therefore they make lechi etc. for it implies he deals with the law of lechi without tzurat hapetach and this is not so; and below siman 362 seif 26 it is explained explicitly that this refers to tzurat hapetach that we make. And in that responsum: nevertheless it is astonishing that he saw that smearing plaster smeared on the wall sometimes comes to ruin because dogs are accustomed to rub against walls and erase the plaster smearing from the walls below more than three toward the ground and it is no longer fit for lechi nor partition for it is a partition that goats penetrate — end of his words; it implies that in any case in this smearing there must be some actual substance and somewhat thick and it does not suffice with the appearance of plaster visible on the wall alone; and so too in that responsum initially that at least it must be thick like a cloak cord; and so too Beit Yosef in the name of responsum of Ra'osh that part of it must protrude — I wrote this because I saw one teacher who commanded to mark on the wall in place of lechi with a type of white earth called kreid — and he erred greatly in this, especially in this matter of plaster smearing that does not fit the law well as Terumat HaDeshen himself wrote there that he strained to uphold the practice in this; and do not add to it — there is only folly and nonsense in this:
8:_: From asherah wood — valid. Beit Yosef wrote: and according to Maharam who holds that cloak cord specifically — do not question from that we validate asherah wood for cut down its measure; one answer: that which requires cloak cord is not because it requires measure but because it must be fit to place something on it — and asherah is also fit to place on it etc.; another answer: the reason of cut down measure is because it stands for burning and since it is possible that it will burn and become ash if one kneads and makes from it a pillar it helps as lechi — end of his words; and I am astonished that a whole mishnah at the end of Temurah was hidden from him: all that are burned — their ash is permitted except asherah wood; and as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 142 that ash of asherah is forbidden in benefit — if so one must scatter it to the wind and the ash is like the wood itself:
9:_: Whether the protrusion is visible to those inside etc. — in the Gemara it is stated first this matter: visible to those inside and equal outside, and likewise the reverse — it is judged as lechi; and Rashi explained: visible inside — he placed the lechi its width toward the length of the mavo and did not draw somewhat of its width outward but equalized its outer edge to the thickness of the walls of the mavo and is like one who adds to the width of the walls and is not visible from outside as lechi but its inner edge is visible inside; visible outside and equal inside — meaning he drew all the lechi outward and the inner edge enters the walls of the mavo and is not visible inside but only appears like adding to the length of the wall but from outside it is recognizable that it is not from the wall of the mavo since it extends beyond the width of the wall etc.; and afterward a baraita of R' Chiyya is stated: a wall one of whose sides is indented from its fellow — whether visible outside and equal inside or the reverse — it is judged as lechi; and Rashi explained another matter: indented — the building receded and reduced its width — now it protrudes and extends like a kind of pillar called piler — whether its indentation is visible inside etc. that the wall recedes behind it and the inner part is visible inside; whether visible outside and equal inside such as the wall recedes from before it so the indentation is not visible to those behind it but relative to reshut ha-rabbim — end of his words; and Beit Yosef wrote regarding Rashi's second explanation: it must read that the side of the wall that was toward the mavo is called behind the wall and the side of the wall outside the mavo is called the face of the wall — end of his words; and the explanation is very astonishing: why should the side of the hollow of the mavo be called behind the wall; for Tosafos question on Rashi's first explanation that if visible outside is considered when the lechi is toward the inner side — how do they answer below that small walls enter etc.; and according to Beit Yosef's explanation in the second explanation it would also question on the second explanation; perforce it appears the difference is between the explanations in this: according to the first explanation it would be visible inside in an inner L-shape and visible outside in a square U-shape — it turns out in both the lechi is not at the edge of the wall on the side of the mavo for this does not help as Tosafos' question; rather they agree with the second explanation and it is in this manner: the face of the wall is called that side facing reshut ha-rabbim — namely the very head of the wall; and behind the wall are called the sides in the wall; perforce visible inside is when there is a flaw in behind the wall — namely the side toward the mavo in an L-shape — and it is exactly like the first explanation and visible outside is when there is a flaw in the face of the wall that is the upper head in a chet-form — this helps specifically since the lechi is not toward the hollow of the mavo for then there is not much recognition but appears like a long wall; and this is explained in Mordechai that wrote there are two explanations in Rashi on visible outside; and according to Beit Yosef there would also be two explanations in visible inside of Rashi's explanation; but certainly as I explained thus Rashi is correct; and I also saw other paths; and in my humble opinion I wrote; and see seif 13:
12:_: If the lechi protrudes into it four amot. Rashi explained: since the permitted length of mavo is released thereby in general and it is called mavo — likewise here even if they made it for the sake of lechi it would be valid because of its closure it is not less than lechi mashehu; here since they did not establish it for lechi in our thought we cannot remove it from the law of wall and make it lechi — since it is removed from the law of lechi it turns out there is no correction for this mavo and another lechi is required to permit the mavo — end of his words; and since Rashi stated that in thought we do not remove it from the law of mavo it implies perforce that it requires in actuality — namely making it initially for the sake of lechi and it does not help with lechi standing by itself and they relied on it on erev Shabbat; and he relied on this count even though with small lechi it is valid; and so too Tosafos that Beit Yosef brings that wrote when he placed it for the sake of lechi it has publicity and recognition; and nevertheless Tur and Shulchan Aruch wrote this law even with relying on it; and in Beit Yosef it is written that from Rashi and Tosafos it implies that with relying it is as if he placed it explicitly — and Beit Yosef left Tur's words in doubt and it is without precision: in some Shulchan Aruch it is written here Rama gloss but there was no lechi and it is a printer's error — its place is before this seif:
13:_: Lechi extending along the side of the mavo. — meaning along the length of the mavo; and in this manner the law applies even if established for lechi — for even though before this it was permitted meaning it protrudes into the width of the mavo and its closure is preferable to lechi mashehu; unlike here where it does not close and whatever four amot — there is no law of lechi even if established for lechi; but less than four amot is valid for this is visible outside and equal inside; and this law is not in Tur only in the Gemara according to Tosafos' explanation and here it implies we do not hold like Tosafos' words that we mentioned in seif 9 that we do not say in such a case visible outside and equal inside that it is lechi:
15:_: And it is required that he place it. — korah is for recognition and there is no recognition here; but lechi is for partition — therefore it helps above with standing by itself:
18:א: That are not a tefach in width. — for otherwise the supports would be considered as korah themselves and not in their length three so that the korah be alone to the wall; and this is explained in seif 25:
18:ב: That must be strong. — in Tur it is also written: if one was of straw of reeds — invalid; it appears to me he needed to write this for straw and reeds are not severed because of the weight of half a brick but because it is soft and thin it is compressed and bent and it is possible the bending reaches an invalid place and even if it does not sever entirely nevertheless invalid:
22:_: Within a tefach. — and even though the law of lavud is up to three — here it is different: zil hakah leika shiyura and zil hakah leika shiyura:
24:_: Somewhat below ten. — in Tur likewise only the word somewhat is not written there; and Beit Yosef explained: it appears that when the korah is placed above ten it deals — but if placed below ten even if its width is not more than required — invalid as Mahari wrote etc.; and his words are not understood; for it is obvious that korah below ten is invalid; and when its width above ten goes until below ten — obviously it is valid for here one need not take anything like with bent — but all this is not the topic here that one makes a wide korah from above downward for korah qualification — this matter he is not dealing with; and nevertheless it is obvious that Beit Yosef's intent is not to tie the permission of this thing specifically to what is below ten; for certainly if above ten it is preferable; rather he said that the head of the korah must be above ten; and Mahari Chalavah disagrees with Beit Yosef and wrote that he understood that the concern is in what part of it is below ten and not above ten — and it is not so; rather one must erase the mem of above ten and it must read ten — meaning the partition is ten — and in the abbreviations he also wrote like here there is a printing error only it must read ten — that is the measure of partition — perforce his words; and in truth Beit Yosef did not intend this and heaven forbid to say it would be judged as korah more when reaching below ten than when reaching above ten; rather regarding prohibition Beit Yosef said thus that the head of the korah should not be below ten — and this is a matter that could not be written here; and the main point is there is no printing error neither in Tur nor in the abbreviations except to amplify they said thus for when the korah is above ten obviously it is valid as korah for behold korah is not nullified there because of partition for there is no partition above ten at all; and this even for Rashba is valid for he said korah that leans below nineteen is invalid — it teaches us that above nineteen is valid — perforce Ra'osh and Tur said it is not so but even if it reaches until below ten and one would say there is partition here and korah is nullified — it teaches us that korah is not nullified there because of its size since the korah is visible — all this is obvious and nothing to emend here; and I wonder at Rashba's view on this; and what Magen Avraham cited from Rashi in seif 12 regarding lechi protruding into the mavo that korah is not nullified because it is large if made for lechi initially — what difference is there here regarding korah that we should not say thus:
26:א: Spaced. — and in the conclusion metsumtsamot — and in both we go stringently:
26:ב: It is not permitted by korah. — for korah is for recognition and above twenty there is no recognition for the eye does not rule over it; but lechi helps for we hold lechi is for partition even though the mavo is very high it is not needed:
26:ג: Must hollow etc. — the reason it does not suffice with a tefach like above twenty — Rashi explained: there it is stated for the side that is already called a side only needs to reduce somewhat for slight recognition suffices; but here that now he makes it a side — less than ten is not called a side — it requires that this side be visible to the measure of mavo qualification:
26:ד: And some disagree on this. — they are Rif and Rambam who hold that since they are open to each other it is as if all are one courtyard and mavo requires two courtyards open into it; the first view is Ra'osh and Tur Mordechai and Rashba shows where he erred here:
26:ה: They have the law of courtyards. — accordingly we would need to correct a pas of four on one side or two mashehuyin on each side as above in courtyard — but it appears they are not accustomed to do so because of open mavo that requires specifically tzurat hapetach:
26:ו: And perforce one must beware etc. — and it appears since one must place reeds below at height ten, one need not tie the rope above on the reeds but may tie the rope even on the roof from this side and that, since the essence of tzurat hapetach is from the reeds below; also from the Gemara we conclude that the upper reed need not touch the reeds — if so perforce it is tied elsewhere; and one need not beware now how the rope is tied on the side of the reeds — for above siman 362 seif 11 we said it does not help — meaning there those reeds themselves are the reeds for tzurat hapetach or there are also reeds above — namely above from the roof and below other reeds — in this one must beware they are in place of doorposts and the way of an opening is only the lintel on the doorposts; unlike if above there are no reeds — only tzurat hapetach through reeds placed below at height ten for tzurat hapetach and above tied on the roof since one cannot place long reeds there from the rope to the ground — then one need not beware how it is tied above on roofs but only that they stand aligned under the rope — for behold there are no doorposts but only what is below at height ten and it is considered as if the rope rests on them literally as stated above to decide this rabbinic matter: and it appears further that if above the reeds placed below there is a roof interrupting between the height of the rope and the reeds there is prohibition in this for it is not tzurat hapetach since the roof interrupts between the rope and the reeds — and we do not make tzurat hapetach in this manner except one must open a large hole in the roof above the reeds in a manner that they are aligned under the rope without interruption; and above I wrote in seif 7 regarding lechi from smeared plaster: and it appears further that if under the rope on the wall projections extend up to ten tefachim near the ground — one may well rely on them on erev Shabbat in place of lechi reeds; and likewise the projections must be exposed above under the rope as in this matter:
29:_: Lest the sea rise as a sandbar. — it will be explained in the responsum that I answered to the community of Steinitz — this is the text of the question: in the community of Steinitz in the land of Mehrin they practiced moving objects on Shabbat without an eruv relying on the city being surrounded by a river around and they acquired permission from the lord — is it fit to do so or not. Answer: it appears it is not correct to do so for two reasons. The first is explicit in the Gemara and poskim and the second although not explicit is nevertheless clearly proven in the Gemara and poskim. The explicit reason is stated in Eruvin daf 8: R' Yehuda — an incident of a mavo one of whose sides ends at the sea and one at a public garbage heap — the matter came before Rabbi and he said neither prohibition nor permission; prohibition he did not say for partitions stand; permission he did not say lest the garbage heap be removed and the sea rise as a sandbar; Rashi explained sandbar of sand and stones at its bank for such is its way and the width of the sea shortens and ground of a parsah or more is made; Beit Yosef in Orach Chayim siman 363 in the name of Magen Avraham Meirat Einayim wrote we are concerned lest the sea rise as a sandbar; and there is dispute among poskim whether we hold this concern — as explained in siman 363 and Beit Yosef ruled to be lenient and Rama brought the stringent view — if so certainly you should be stringent in this concern lest part of the waters at its bank be covered by sand and stones and they carry there. Second: it appears here all hold to prohibition even though they said at the end of the thrower in tractate Shabbos daf 100: a pit in reshut ha-rabbim ten deep and four wide full of water — if one threw into it he is liable; full of fruits — if one threw into it he is exempt — why? water does not nullify partition; fruits nullify partition etc. — it teaches us that through water partition is not nullified; nevertheless since the way of water here is to freeze and ice in cold season — behold at those times there is no partition at all and it is obvious forbidden to carry; and this concern does not apply to sea that does not freeze; but in that of making pasin 4:22 in what Magen Avraham wrote surrounding it the Euphrates on this side: and one should not learn permission from the mishnah of chapter Window (Eruvin daf 78) that taught: a ditch between two courtyards ten deep and four wide — they make two eruvin and not one; even full of straw or hay, full of earth or stones — they make one eruv and not two etc. — it teaches us that through filling with straw partitions are not nullified since he will take the straw from there for his animal — likewise we would say since frozen water will eventually melt and become flowing water as at first partitions are not nullified; and one may say on this: perhaps here it is different since freezing happens by itself not by human action unlike filling with straw; if so perhaps it helps here what will eventually be removed; but there is no question for behold we find in chapter He May Not Dig (Bava Batra daf 20) regarding reduction of window that brings there: he removed grass and placed it in the window or grass that grew by itself in the window — it is not reduction; behold before you that growing by itself has no advantage to nullify more than coming there by human action; and likewise we may say freezing of water is considered as if the pit were filled with straw that does not nullify the pit; but all this is not so for Tosafos there in chapter Window explained that filling with straw that does not nullify partition is because that straw is taken on Shabbat and is not muktzeh; and they bring proof from what we say there afterward that even a pouch nullifies a person etc.; and that fruits nullify partition even though taken on Shabbat is d'oraisa and certainly nullifies; but for eruv which is rabbinic one may distinguish between taken on Shabbat and not taken on Shabbat — perforce we learn from this that whatever is certainly there on Shabbat — forbidden to take from there such as straw prepared for bricks not for animal feed — is called certainly nullification of partition and even though certainly afterward he will take it — nevertheless every Shabbat this is called nullification of partition; likewise here and all the more since frozen water will certainly stand all Shabbat; and further proof from chapter Window (Eruvin daf 77a): Rav Yechiel covered a bowl — meaning adjacent to the wall and reduced the height of the wall less than ten from the bowl to the head of the wall from his reduction; and they challenge there: and why — it is taken on Shabbat; and they answer: it is not needed for he attached it to the ground for that bowl and they will not move it on Shabbat; and they challenge: what difference from muktzeh that he hid in straw that is forbidden to take on Shabbat if part of it is not exposed; and they answer: it is not needed for we require recognition and a basket; behold before us that specifically what is fit to take on that Shabbat is not considered to nullify partition; but not what is forbidden to take on Shabbat even though certainly he will take it after Shabbat through recognition and basket — nevertheless now it is considered nullification of partition; if so all the more here since freezing is accustomed to stand many weeks on the water; and further proof for prohibition from the initial enactment that the Rabbis enacted recognition in lechi and korah for closed mavo from three sides — Rashi explained at the beginning of Eruvin in the first mishnah: the Rabbis decreed in mavo lest they confuse with complete reshut ha-rabbim; and likewise in karmelit the Rabbis decreed on them lest they confuse with reshut ha-yachid as stated chapter 1 of Shabbos daf 6; and all our domains are karmelit as all poskim wrote — if so here when water freezes and people walk there like in the rest of the city and sometimes snow covers until the water underneath is not recognizable at all — it is obvious the Rabbis decreed more lest they confuse with reshut ha-rabbim for there is no recognition at all here. And one may say: only on those Shabbatot when water freezes would carrying be forbidden in the entire city; but on other Shabbatot not — this is not so for we said in that of concerned lest sea rise sandbar that I brought above that Rabbi did not wish to say permission even though partitions stand from the reason lest sometimes there be no partition there — all the more here that most of the year certainly there is decree even all year because of those Shabbatot; and further proof from mishnah of chapter Window (Eruvin daf 78) regarding ditch — if one placed a board four wide — if they wish they make one eruv; and from this one may not learn permission; for if they freeze in rainy season partition is nullified and forbidden to carry; and see in responsum of Chacham Tzvi siman 37; (and see in Even HaEzer who expanded to prove frozen water does not nullify partitions — see there in Maginei Eretz printing Propes): however if on the riverbank on dry land there is a slope ten high over four amot as written siman 366 — we consider that slope in place of a partition, end of his words:
30:_: Except opposite the short side. — meaning it is forbidden to place it diagonally and use the long side — Rava holds korah diagonally is not recognition; Rashi explained: those viewing the people of the mavo extend and use reshut ha-rabbim outside except opposite the short wall; or: permitted to use reshut ha-rabbim according to what is not like that part of the mavo — end of his words; and nevertheless the reason appears permitted diagonally within the mavo since there one will not err in permission in reshut ha-rabbim; and this is specifically when there is not more than ten in the diagonal for the Gemara said when more than ten all hold he does not place opposite the short but diagonally; but within ten we hold like Rava who said opposite the short; and accordingly within the mavo Rava also permits diagonally — this also within ten thus appeared initially; except Shulchan Aruch and Tur wrote but if he wishes he may make tzurat hapetach diagonally within the mavo — he may; it implies within the mavo equals tzurat hapetach and tzurat hapetach even in width more than ten; and Beit Yosef wrote on outside the mavo that tzurat hapetach helps and it appears initially likewise for lechayim for we hold lechi is for partition; and straightly; but two lechayim placed one opposite the other diagonally — permitted to use until opposite the lechayim diagonally provided there is not more than ten between the lechayim etc.; and it is possible that even though lechayim are for partition they do not help like tzurat hapetach etc. — end of his words; and Mahari Chalavah wrote plainly that when there is not more than ten lechayim help as explained shortly afterward; but if they made in the middle two pasin etc. — it teaches that similar to tzurat hapetach; and what Raavad wrote here that tzurat hapetach helps even in width ten — meaning to say even in width ten it helps unlike two lechayim; and not like Beit Yosef's conclusion that lechayim do not help — and it is an error regarding him for certainly they help even diagonally — end of his words; and in my humble opinion even doubt there is none as Beit Yosef thought; rather it is simple they do not help at all for whenever lechayim do not stand equally they are not this matter to each other; that one standing at the short side itself permits carrying in the mavo until opposite it straight and no more outward; and that lechi standing at the long side neither helps nor hurts for it does not permit opposite it for behold opposite it is only reshut ha-rabbim; if so it is only like an ordinary tree and what would the lechi opposite the short help him and it has no partnership with him and the short side does not need it; unlike korah placed diagonally from this to that — the partnership is visible to the eyes that one goes from this to that; unlike two lechayim where the one outside does not need its fellow and permits opposite itself well alone and it alone for partition — we view as if a partition spread equally opposite it and the partition has no connection with the second; and I would say regarding what is written shortly that two lechayim permit in the middle of the mavo — there they stand straight and each needs its fellow in order to divide domains and there specifically two are required as written shortly; unlike here diagonally and even within the mavo permitted here with korah diagonally — nevertheless if one made two pasin diagonally there is no partnership but that closer to outside itself permits opposite itself and the second is without need — all this appears clear and there is not even doubt for permission:
31:א: If there is a courtyard etc. — for then the people of that courtyard forbid into the mavo on those who wish to make eruv for themselves; and if the outer ones did not make lechi at the side of reshut ha-rabbim they were not fit to make eruv at all with the inner one since the mavo was not qualified from their side — they cannot forbid the others for one does not forbid one another unless all are one domain and they can make eruv together:
31:ב: But if they made in the middle etc. — this is not regarding permission to carry inward; if so one lechi suffices as at the head of the mavo; rather they came here to divide domains so the outer ones separate from the inner and do not forbid them — tzurat hapetach or two pasin is required; meaning mashehu from here and mashehu from here and it is as if an actual partition between them; for specifically for permission to carry one suffices not for dividing domains — thus Ra'osh's reasoning here:
33:א: And he places it in the middle. — meaning in the middle of the opening:
33:ב: And every condition of mavo etc. — thus it should read and not as some books wrote condition of courtyard:
33:ג: And what is from the pas until the wall etc. — in Hagahot Ashiri and Tur it is written if there is from the pas to the middle wall of the mavo more than ten amot etc.; and Beit Yosef wrote I do not know why he wrote thus for even if there is not more than ten between them its law is like crooked mavo that its law is like open — and see siman 365 seif 2; and I wonder at Ra'osh how he was silent and at Rabbeinu and R' Yeruham who did not notice this — end of his words; and nevertheless Shulchan Aruch did not write here more than ten like Tur's wording but Rama wrote it in the wording of some say; and Mahari Chalavah resolved Tur's words with great strain and I wondered at Beit Yosef's wonder on this for certainly in actual crooked mavo as in siman 364 whose form is thus — there we say that even if there is not more than ten in its bends its law is like open — for Rav and such we hold; unlike here where we make one mavo going equally as two mavo'ot — namely through pas of four in length four amot — and we have to say these two mavo'ot go equally until the middle wall and here there is no crooked mavo at all for the opening open downward from the pas is an opening from one mavo to its fellow — if so its law is like two mavo'ot one to another and there is an opening from one to its fellow — perforce they wrote if there is more than ten from the pas to the middle wall as Tosafos wrote in Beit Yosef that wrote if from the head of the pas of the inner side until the middle wall there is more than ten — tzurat hapetach is required for it is like crooked mavo etc.; behold it is explained that thereby since there is no law of opening on it it becomes crooked mavo; unlike crooked mavo in siman 364 whose form and building was literally in the bend and need not make it crooked; and I wondered Beit Yosef did not notice this for it is a simple matter in my humble opinion; and if so here too it is fit to emend thus that there is more than ten from the pas to the wall like Tur:
34:_: And he makes a pas three amot wide etc. — the rule in this is that the pas must be greater than the airspace between it and the wall; if not the airspace of this side and that side comes and nullifies the pas:
36:_: Within four amot. — meaning within four amot there is height ten — it is as reshut ha-yachid; but if within five — behold it is like other reshut ha-rabbim for its use is for walking:
